text:
RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 5

Both you and the successful candidate are women, so sex can't easily explain why she was chosen over you. An all-female panel is also unremarkable in itself — single-sex panels occur routinely by chance, and in many fields women are well represented on hiring committees. Raising it would look like grasping, and would undermine your credible complaint.

Your real grievance is substantive: a candidate with fewer formal qualifications was preferred, and you've had no written reasons after two weeks. Most public universities are legally or administratively obliged to give reasons. Send a dated follow-up, citing the relevant regulation or collective agreement, and ask specifically how "industry experience" was weighted against publications and teaching. Escalate to the ombudsman if ignored.
